_notes: The house around a friar, one line most weeks, as the parish's ambient lines are around a pastor (content/parish/ambient.json). Pools: any; the season; the house's kind; formation (not yet ordained) or priest; and order:<key>, the order's own customs (the Salve and the O Lumen, the cappa, the Rule read at table), drawn twice as often. Lines never name the prior, since the man reading them may be the prior, and never name a real friar or institution (CLAUDE.md rule 13). systems/religious/houseLife.ts picks a pool, then a line, and will not repeat a line the Record shows from the last twelve weeks.
any: The refectory reading this week is a life of a missionary bishop, and the lector cannot pronounce any of the place names.
Someone has left the good coffee in the community room with a note that says it is for everyone. By Wednesday it is gone.
The bell for Lauds rang four minutes late on Tuesday. Nobody said anything at breakfast, which is how the house says something.
A box of books from a dead friar's room sits in the corridor outside the library, waiting for someone to decide what they are worth.
The house car came back from the garage with a bill the procurator read twice.
Recreation ran long on Thursday over an argument about a baseball trade that none of the men involved will admit to having started.
A brother from another house stayed two nights on his way somewhere and left the guest room neater than he found it.
The chapter room chairs have been reupholstered. The old men say the new ones are too soft for a chapter.
The door to the enclosure sticks again. Three men have fixed it this year, each in his own way.
The laundry list on the notice board has been reorganized by someone who will not sign his name to it.
Two of the older men have stopped speaking at table over a point of liturgy, and the rest of the house is careful where it sits.
The mail brought a letter for a friar who died nine years ago. It is from his nephew, who did not know.
The house cook made the soup the old men like, and there was a second helping for everyone, and nobody mentioned the budget.
A thunderstorm took the power out during Compline, and the house finished it by memory in the dark, most of it correctly.
The province's newsletter came. Everyone read the obituaries first and the appointments second.
The garden has come up in tomatoes nobody planted, and the house has decided they are a sign of something.
advent: The Advent wreath in the refectory leans a little further every week, and the house has decided to let it.
The O antiphons at Vespers this week, and the novices have been practicing them in the stairwell.
The crib figures came down from the attic missing a shepherd, as they have for eleven years.
christmas: The house kept Christmas with a long dinner and a longer recreation, and the old men sang songs from their novitiate that nobody else knew.
Families of the men sent cookies from four states. The tins are stacked on the community room table in the order they arrived.
Midnight Mass in the priory church was fuller than the house expected, and the ushers were two friars who had never ushered.
lent: Lenten table: silence at supper and a reading from the desert fathers, which the house finds harder than the fast.
The house gave up dessert for Lent, except on Sundays, which the procurator says costs more than dessert.
The Stations of the Cross on Friday evening drew more people from the street than the house expected, and fewer friars.
holy_week: Holy Week: the house moves from the chapel to the church and back, and the sacristan has not slept since Palm Sunday.
The washing of the feet in the refectory on Thursday. The oldest man in the house insisted on doing it himself, on his knees.
The house kept the watch at the altar of repose in pairs through the night, and the sign-up sheet filled by breakfast.
easter: Easter Week: the house has permission to talk at breakfast, and it does.
The paschal candle is taller than last year's, and the sacristan has been asked twice who approved the expense.
The Easter Vigil ran three hours and ten minutes. The house has a pool on it every year; the winner was a novice.
priory: The priory's parlor had a visitor every afternoon this week, and every one of them asked for a particular friar by name.
A benefactor of the priory came to lunch and stayed through Vespers, and the house was very polite to him.
The priory's roof leaked into the choir during the Office. A bucket sat in the stalls through the Magnificat.
studium: The studium's examination schedule went up on the notice board, and the library was full until midnight all week.
A lector and a student argued about grace in the corridor outside the classroom for an hour, and a small crowd gathered.
The studium's reading room lost its heating again. The students study in their coats, which the lectors say is traditional.
novitiate: The novices painted the barn this week, as novices have painted it every year since the house was built. It is the same colour.
A novice's family visited on Sunday, and his mother cried at Vespers, and the house pretended not to notice.
Manual labour this week was the orchard: the novices came back to supper scratched, sunburned, and very quiet.
parish: The parish office phone rang through the Office twice this week, and both times it was about a baptism date.
The parish's festival committee met in the friary's parlor and did not leave until the house had eaten.
A parishioner left a casserole on the friary doorstep with a note that said only, for the fathers.
school: The school's basketball team won on Friday, and two of the friars went to the game in their habits and were cheered.
Report cards went home this week. Three parents asked to speak with a friar, and none of them wanted to speak about grades.
The school's chapel was full for the first Friday Mass, because the principal took attendance.
mission: The mission's clinic ran out of antibiotics on Wednesday, and a friar drove four hours to the city and back for them.
The rains came and the road washed out, and the house ate what was in the storeroom for three days.
A catechist walked two days from a village to ask for a priest for a feast, and the house found one.
curia: The curia's photocopier broke during the preparation for the provincial council, and three friars learned it could be fixed with a coat hanger.
Letters from every house in the province came through the curia this week, and the secretary read them all aloud at supper, with commentary.
The province's archivist found the minutes of a chapter from before the war and has been quoting them at recreation.
formation: A student a year ahead of you failed his examination in moral theology and is taking it again in a month, and the whole corridor is helping.
The house's formation team met on Thursday. Nobody knows what they said, and everyone has a theory.
One of the men in your class has been going to chapel at four in the morning. Nobody asks him why, but everyone knows.
A man two years ahead of you asked for a leave of absence. His room was empty by Saturday, and his name was not said at table.
The students' common room got a new couch, donated by somebody's aunt, and it is already the subject of a rota.
priest: Your Mass intentions are written in a ledger in the sacristy now, and the stipends go into the house's account without passing through your hands.
A priest of the diocese came to the friary to confess, as he does every month, because he says the friars do not know him.
The weekend supply schedule came out. You are at a parish forty minutes away on the second Sunday, and the pastor has asked for a short homily.
Someone from the neighborhood rang the friary bell at eleven at night for a priest, and the man on call went.
A couple whose wedding you did last year sent a photograph of the baby with a note asking when you could baptize him.
order:OP: The Salve after Compline: the procession to the Lady altar, the holy water from the hebdomadary, and the O Lumen for Dominic, the novices a half beat behind.
Someone left a copy of the Summa open on the refectory lectern at the article on whether God exists, which is either a joke or a hint.
A lay Dominican in a white scapular over a cardigan asked at the door for the friar who gives the Thursday talks, and was given tea.
The fifteen-decade rosary on a novice's belt caught in the choir stall again, and the whole side waited while he freed it.
The black cappa came out of the closets for the first cold Sunday, and the parish children stared as if the friars had turned into crows.
The province's newsletter reports three friars preaching missions in three states, and a fourth who has been asked back to the same parish for the ninth year.
A diocesan priest at the door wanted to borrow a volume of the Leonine edition, and the librarian made him sign for it in two places.
The disputation at recreation, on whether a friar may keep a dog, went to the dog, on the ground that Dominic's mother dreamed of one.
The Rosary Confraternity's list in the sacristy has grown by a page; the sacristan enrolls the names and a friar blesses the beads on Saturdays.
The syndic went over the house accounts at council and read out, without comment, how much the house spends on books.
The Master of the Order's letter to the friars was read at table: on preaching, on study, and on the brothers who are tired, which silenced the refectory.
A student brother preached at Compline for the first time, seven minutes on the Magnificat, and the lector who taught him homiletics nodded once.
The nuns of the order sent their Christmas cards early, one to each friar by name, with a line saying they pray for the preachers.
Somebody said Veritas at dinner as a joke, and the table argued for an hour about whether it is a motto or a demand.
The house's Friday talk on the Summa drew forty people: engineers, a retired judge, two students, and a woman who takes notes in shorthand.
A friar back from the province's mission band slept eleven hours and then preached the Sunday Mass as if he had never left.
order:OSA: Someone read Augustine's Rule aloud at table, the part about not letting the sun set on anger, and two brothers who had quarrelled looked at their plates.
The house kept its evening of conversation in common, which the Rule asks for and the house takes seriously, and it ran past ten.
A letter from a friend in another house arrived and was answered the same evening; the Augustinians keep their friendships in ink.
The Confessions on the refectory lectern this month, book eight, and the garden in Milan; the novices stopped eating to listen.
The black habit and the leather belt came out for the school's opening Mass, and the freshmen looked at the friars as if they were history.
One heart and one soul toward God, the Rule says; the house council spent an hour on the car rota trying to live up to it.
Someone from the school asked whether St. Monica's day is a holiday, and was told it is a day for mothers to be prayed for, which is better.
The brothers' common purse paid for a trip home for a friar whose mother is failing, and nobody asked what it cost.
